# Headless, handoff and subagent component trace

Oracle: Go source 21d0bc7935a2c4696fb89ccff2e324157a528c2d. No production Go or Web
source is changed by these ports or fixtures. Session/Hub caller integration and
native provider acceptance are separate gates; these component APIs are real
implementations, not successful substitutes for unimplemented callers.

## Source → implementation → tests

- `internal/headless/{adapter,prompt}.go` → `orchestration/headless.rs`:
  registry/argv/prompt/EOF contracts in `headless_contracts`.
- `internal/headless/{event,format_text,format_claude_stream_json}.go` →
  `headless_formats.rs`: actual-Go 60-case parser/event/render corpus generated by
  `../headless/oracle.go`, plus format validation and a 40-case actual-Go
  byte-framing corpus across four input chunk divisions (including boundary CRs).
- `internal/headless/runner.go` → `headless.rs` using shared `ManagedProcess`:
  synthetic child executable verifies duplex output-before-input, large prompt,
  stdin EOF, nonzero exit overriding model success, model failure not overriding
  exit zero, timeout, cancellation including already-closed pipes, oversized line
  drainage, inherited descendant pipes, explicit broadcast lag, private opt-in
  RuntimePaths logs, invalid format and missing executable errors.
- `internal/handoff/{handoff,render}.go` → `handoff.rs`:
  actual-Go 7-case render/sanitize corpus, exact 21-field allowlist, per-line v1 stamping,
  unknown kinds, nullable/case-folded Go decoding, corrupt-line recovery,
  concurrent append, private modes, historical-byte and open-handle preservation,
  retention/stat, root/leaf symlink rejection, and failed rendered-file replacement
  preserving source records.
- `internal/hub/subagent_source_claude.go` → `subagent/claude.rs`:
  nested/orphan/workflow filtering, allowed tool summaries only, sticky
  foreground/background launch and completion latches, all unsuccessful terminal
  statuses, unchanged metadata/file caching, measured child head/tail bounds,
  incomplete final records, cutoff and oldest-completed tree-cap behavior.
- `internal/hub/subagent_source_codex.go` → `subagent/codex.rs`:
  first-line metadata discovery, transitive root connection, at most 32 day
  directories, old-day scan cache, sticky SubAgentActivity lifecycle,
  once-only unknown/freshness fallback, custom-tool versus function-call summary,
  bounded child tails and unrelated candidate exclusion.
- `internal/hub/subagent_source_grok.go` → `subagent/grok.rs`:
  parent updates plus fixed metadata, sticky launch/completion, sibling
  child-session flat event records (never nonexistent subagents/id/events),
  metadata parent validation, no rawInput/output/prompt/error fields, safe path
  component validation, and terminal-cache reuse.
- `internal/hub/subagent_tree.go` → `subagent.rs`:
  typed adapter/continuation dispatch, exact SHA256 signature fields including
  last activity but excluding poll time, running-count cutoff, reattach
  state/cutoff preservation with dedupe reset, and generation rejection.

`go-input.json` is a synthetic file-tree specification. `regenerate.py` loads
`oracle_test.go.txt` through Go's test-only overlay and invokes the actual
unmodified `subagentReaderByKey` implementations to write `go-golden.json`.
Rust reconstructs the same synthetic file trees, timestamps and cutoffs and
compares trees and exact signatures. The overlay is not a rewritten reader.

## Explicit boundaries / safety strengthenings

- `ReadBatch.tree == None` means unavailable/no change. A completed empty scan is
  `Some(empty tree)`, preserving the source's separate attempted-empty clearing
  decision without conflating errors with absence. Caller resolution, timers and
  session incarnation checks are outside this reader module.
- Child head/tail caps are 64/128 KiB, parent tail is 2 MiB/500 records, tree cap
  is 50 nodes, Codex metadata first line is 4 MiB. Small Claude/Grok metadata
  files are defensively rejected above 4 MiB. Incomplete tail records are not
  parsed. Read statistics expose actual accepted read-byte counts.
- Go ReadLine preserves a trailing CR across its 64 KiB buffer boundary; its
  effective maximum pending fragment is 1 MiB + 64 KiB - 1, despite the source
  maxLineBytes name. The Rust framer preserves this behavior and bounded memory.
- Handoff and raw logs use private kernel append handles without reading old log
  bodies. Record writes are serialized in this process; callers own blocking IO
  placement outside session/Hub locks. Rendered files use private atomic
  replacement and retain the source log on failure. All handoff IO uses held
  directory capabilities: render reads and replaces through the same directory;
  retention and stats ignore symlink/nonregular leaves. Native Windows ACL and
  directory-pinning acceptance remain separate from source checks.
- Grok child_session_id cannot contain traversal/separators. Transcript/note/work
  document paths remain strings only and are never opened by handoff rendering.
- Shared process zero timeout means no local deadline. Shared owned-group/job
  cleanup, pipe-drain bound and explicit receiver lag are retained. Stream loss
  produces an error state with actual child exit code still retained; it cannot
  silently become a completed output scan.
- These test executions use synthetic processes/files only. Windows Job setup
  failure/native ACL/ConPTY behavior, native macOS execution, paid provider
  launch, real transcripts, SSH/WSL, actual session/Hub registration/replay/UI
  and copied-user-data acceptance remain unexecuted here.
